Hupalovka (Vesela Yevreyka) Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zaporizhia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Hupalivka — founded in 1845 as Jewish Colony Number 2 in Veselaya — was a genuinely mixed settlement, with 44 Jewish, 7 German, and 1 Russian households recorded in 1893. Sixty-three Jews were murdered during the German occupation, though a Jewish presence persisted in the village after WWII; the village itself was liquidated in 1968 as 'economically unviable,' and its residents were resettled elsewhere. According to a local resident named Sergei, someone dug up a grave here about five years before the ESJF survey, and a broken, Hebrew-inscribed tombstone that had been standing just a couple of years earlier now lies fallen by the road.
